title: Exponential Backoff with Jitter

validation.research: Six primary references: Marc Brooker’s original 2015 AWS backoff/jitter contention analysis; the AWS Builders’ Library retry guidance; official AWS SDK retry behavior including its current 2026 rollout opt-in warning; RFC 6585 section 4 for 429; RFC 9110 sections 9.2.2 and 10.2.3 for retry safety and Retry-After; Python random documentation for inclusive integer uniform draws and seeded generators. Full, equal and decorrelated jitter are distinguished. Retry with Backoff and Jitter is a broader descriptive alias, while the established canonical Exponential Backoff with Jitter title is retained. Independent samples can coincide or decrease; a capped wait is not a finite operation budget or aggregate admission quota. Original worker-recovery, server-delay and uncertain-write contexts are retained and refined. Demo, policy constants, sample timing and native diagrams are original teaching material.

runnable_example.verification: Actual article fences run unchanged. Exact seven-line seeded output, allowances 1000/939/881 ms, waits 41/38 ms, three 20 ms callbacks and 139 ms elapsed. Success and falsy results require no randomness or wait. Lower and upper inclusive draws verify windows 0..100, 0..200, 0..400, four attempts total, three waits maximum, unchanged last failure and no terminal wait. Permanent/unclassified ValueError, PermissionError and TimeoutError retain identity and do not trigger further retries. Deadline equality/overrun during failure, exact/excess wait-fit boundaries and chained eligible errors stop without clamping or sleeping. Zero and just-fitting samples admit only within remaining time. Wake overshoot prevents a next callback; expiry before initial admission starts nothing. Late success is rejected after callback returns, not preempted. Cancellation-like BaseException during read or waiting escapes with no new attempt. Real TemporaryFile resources are closed by the callback before policy waits and after success, verifying the stated ownership precondition rather than claiming policy-driven release. Seeded clients can collide, different seeds vary, and all illustrative consecutive waits satisfy 1/2/4 second bounds. No live network, wall-clock timing, HTTP/Retry-After parsing, duplicate protection, aggregate quota, rollback or durable scheduling is inferred.

example_limits: Existing canonical data-exponential-backoff-with-jitter is expanded in place, retaining its title, ID, URL, Data Engineering tags/verse, extraction-worker scenario, original timing-figure asset path, and unchanged historical import provenance. Its one primary collection moves to Reliability and Failure Handling; the former Execution & recovery collection retains a cross-link. Original article and SVG are saved in ignored task evidence. Original Python 3.11+ virtual-time read simulation uses four total attempts, 1000 ms total budget and inclusive integer full-jitter windows 0..100, 0..200, 0..400 ms. Each read receives the remaining allowance and must account for its duration on a nondecreasing supplied clock, releasing resources before return/error. Only TemporaryUnavailable is eligible; other errors/cancellation escape. Seed 7 gives waits 41 and 38 ms, three 20 ms reads, and 139 ms elapsed. No wait follows success/final failure, a sample consuming all remaining time is rejected without clamping, wake overshoot is checked before another call, and late results are rejected without claiming preemption. No actual service, wall-clock sleep, transport cancellation, HTTP parser, Retry-After policy, aggregate quota, remote rollback, duplicate protection or durable scheduler is implemented. Verification also covers falsy successful values, unchanged final eligible failure, inclusive minimum/maximum samples, permanent/unclassified error identity, exact/excess expiry and delay-fit boundaries, zero-delay retry, wake overshoot, expiry before initial admission, late callback returns, cancellation-like BaseException from read/wait, independent and colliding seeded schedules, and real callback-owned TemporaryFile closure before waiting. This confirms the callback cleanup precondition; it does not claim the retry policy closes unknown resources. No actual network, wall-clock sleep, time preemption, HTTP parsing, server-directed-delay policy, durable scheduler, quota, fairness or duplicate-effect safety is implemented.
